review:
Ground Zeroes, when capped at 60fps, is formerly amazing at THIS price tag. It's almost like a rogue-like, a fully "arcade" session of Metal Gear Solid V. Lots, LOTS of options and things to do (but not AS much someone could think of looking at the absolute photo-realism of the enviroenment) if you look forward them. 

I'm not going to talk about the storyline or the heavy importance it has on the Saga, so I'll add one last line: the game is very, VERY "score"-centric, if you don't like to go for multiple runs, records or unlockables, I suggest to wait for a most likely future "GZ + TPP bundle".

It's short, no denying that. As I'm sure you've heard, the game is incredibly short. I knew this going in, and intentionally took my time. I was still able to finish it in an hour and ten minutes. 

Granted, the "story" is supplemented by several side missions (only playable after you finish the story) which range from meeting contacts to rescuing agents, finding intel, destroying facilities, or even assassinating different people (whom you must identify from pictures). All in all, it's several hours of gameplay.

As for the gameplay itself? Honestly, it's pretty fantastic. Combat is tight, stealth is difficult and rewarding, from what I've seen, the AI is very smart and pretty perceptive, none of that "hide three feet from their face" you get from "stealth" in games like Skyrim. If you aren't hidden, they'll spot you from a hundred yards, and they'll investigate. Very good AI.

The game boasts an "open world", but the open world is a single prison camp on Cuba. The camp is not especially large, and some of the features new to  the Metal Gear franchise are pretty useless as a result, like Snake's new ability to drive vehicles (that said, I did enjoy the AI's use of vehicles in patrols and transportation).

The screenshots look pretty fantastic, right? You'd think that there's no way you could get your rig to do something like that. I'll admit, my computer is pretty decent in regards to gaming, but it often lags behind on newer titles. This game, however? It runs amazingly. Seriously, this might be the best optimized game engine I have ever played. I was getting those graphics at high FPS. Only in a handful of occasions did the game ever stutter, and these events were brief and far between.

For the story quality, there honestly isn't that much. The game is literally, with no exaggeration here, "Go here, get this guy, bring him to the chopper. Go there, get that girl, bring her to the chopper. Cutsene. Credits." At best, it's a demo/prologue of Phantom Pain. At worst, it's an epilogue to Peace Walker. The game takes place right after the end of Peace Walker, and centers around the rescues from a Cuban base of two characters from Peace Walker. The game does include some backstory which you can view, which is nice, but people who played PW (such as myself) will probably appreciate the characters more, and feel the impact of certain events near the end much more.

Now, the final verdict: The game is fantastic, and that only makes it that much more painful that there's so little to enjoy. I'm going to give it a different rating based on the price. If it's on sale for five bucks, I'd say it's a must-buy. If it's on sale for ten, I'd give it some thought. For twenty? A flat-out no, unless you're an absolute die-hard fan. I'm giving it a thumbs up for in general, as it is a good game, but if you aren't able to get it on sale, I'd suggest you just go ahead and skip this one; buy the Phantom Pain when the game is worth the price. Watch a playthrough on Youtube. It'll only take an hour.

The enemy AI in this game is absolutely why I continue to play, and replay this game at least once a week.

When I play stealth games, I'm not interested in learning patrol patterns and sneaking around them with no problem. What I'm really interested in is an AI system that has context and situational awareness. This game has both. The main mission takes place during a hurricane, naturally this gives the AI reduced sight/hearing and what have you. I'll give a very brief example of the AI's contextual awareness.

After getting spotted and going into the, as I understand it, new slow motion 'second chance' system where you can take out the enemy that spotted you and go unnoticed, I shot the unlucky guard in the face with a suppressed weapon. Minutes later I intercept a radio transmission from the control tower the the guard I just took out. From what I can tell each guard is assigned a number 'Delta 1, Delta 2' and so on. Since the guard they were radioing was out of commision, they sent another guard to check on him. Soon they found the body. 

In most stealth games you'd expect them to see the body and then either that guard doesn't tell anybody and searches for you, or other guards that have no idea what happened all know you're there. This game was different.
He assessed the situation and radioed back to the tower that he died of a gunshot wound and since nobody reported hearing one, concluded that the intruder responsible must be using a suppressed weapon. After hearing this information, the entire base went on alert with sirens going off all over the place and backup arriving just a minute later.

Most stealth games these days have me feeling pretty confident that I can hide around a corner and I won't get spotted. This is not the case for Ground Zeroes. If you want to get 20 feet inside this base without getting seen or heard, you need to find a vantage point and survey the area for a good 5 minutes, tagging enemies, trucks, watch towers ect.
This is as true to life as any stealth game I've played has come for me in the past 20 years. If you like MGS, this is worth checking out to get a taste of the Phantom Pain. If you like stealth games, there's enough here to keep you busy without knowing the setting or story.

This is just an example of how advanced this AI is for this type of open world setting. I'm a new fan of the MGS games and other than the Metal Gear Acid 'board games' for the PSP is my first time playing any MGS game. I can already say that without a doubt, I'm buying Phantom Pain when it releases and for stealth lovers, this is a lovely distraction from the wait until Phantom Pain comes out.

As good as [i]The Phantom Pain is[/i], I had more fun with [i]Ground Zeroes[/i]. 

Why is that? 

Whereas [i]The Phantom Pain[/i] is big, bloated, and bogged down by superfluous elements, [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] is tightly focused. Instead of trying to do many things, it only does a few things and does them well. Everything, from the relative simplicity of the gameplay to the open but not "open world" environment, adds to the illusion of being a stealth action hero.

When I play [i]Ground Zeroes[/i], I'm not thinking about checklists, base-building requirements or how long it takes to unlock the absurdly powerful weapon no one needs by the time they get it, all of which carry an unpleasant resemblance to microtransaction-based mobile gaming. I'm thinking about how cool it is to sneak through a base of Marines in the middle of a rainstorm. What's more, I don't feel the need to Fulton extract everything in sight. I can simply focus on the action.

Yes, it's only a prologue. But [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] is a smarter, tighter game. That's all there is to it.

"You've already seen the "Overwhelmingly Positive" user reviews, haven't you? Why are you here, then? Why do you continue to scroll through them while your memory betrays you? You enjoy reading reviews, that's why."

I'll get straight to the point. This review's main goal is to address common misconceptions.

Amount of Content:
Ground Zeroes offers 7 missions: one main story, four side missions with different objectives, two extra side missions that are aimed at the fans of the series. Each mission has two difficulty settings (hard unlocks after beating normal), secret collectibles/objectives and unlockable trials (challenges). Throughout all missions you'll be dealing with only one location: Camp Omega, which is a fairly large facility. Each mission has it's own time of day.
If you like playing your games at a medium pace and you never had contact with this game before then you'll be able to complete all 7 missions in 5-10 hours+. If you're willing to spend time to get 100% completion, get most of the rewards and read/listen to the story then you might end up with 15-20 hours+ on you. However, it's possible to speedrun all 7 mission in ~1 hour (that is, if you know what you're doing). If you buy Phantom Pain alone then you won't be able to access Camp Omega and it's missions through it as they're avilable only for those that purchased Ground Zeroes (meaning this is a prologue and not a demo). However, if you purchased both then you'll be able to visit Camp Omega with all your Phantom Pain upgrades, not to mention special bonuses.

Performance & Settings:
Runs on systems that are below minimum system requirements. Well optimized, but could've had even higher level of detail / drawing distance settings (some visible popup of small items). One common complaint are increased amounts of depth of field (blur / out of focus). It's easily "fixed" by decreasing Screen Filtering to High.
Fully playable on K&M but could've had a slightly better control scheme (currently there's some sensitivty bug when aiming while zoomed). Minority of people experiences some compatibility issues some of which were caused by bad system configurations, but some are legit and there most likely will be a compatibility fixing patch.

[b]Before the massive epic that is METAL GEAR SOLID V: The Phantom Pain, Kojima gave us Ground Zeroes. While many people debated whether this should have been a DLC or a standalone release, one thing is certain: this short game delivers pure Kojima magic in every second of its runtime.
It may only last a couple of hours, but it serves as a perfect prologue and gameplay showcase of what was to come. For me, it was an unforgettable experience.[/b]

[h1]Gameplay & Stealth Mechanics:[/h1]
[b]Ground Zeroes refines the Metal Gear formula into a modern stealth sandbox.[/b]
[list]
[*][u]Freedom of Approach:[/u] Infiltrate Camp Omega your way, sneaking through shadows, using silenced weapons, distracting guards, or going full guns blazing (if you’re brave enough).

[*][u]Improved Controls:[/u] Compared to earlier MGS titles, controls feel smoother, more responsive, and intuitive, making stealth much more satisfying.

[*][u]Replay Value:[/u] While the main mission is short, side ops and challenges add layers of replayability for those who love experimenting with different tactics.
[/list]
[b]This is two hours of gameplay that you’ll want to replay multiple times just to experience everything it offers.[/b]

[h1]Story & Atmosphere:[/h1]
[b]The narrative is short but emotionally impactful, serving as a direct lead into The Phantom Pain. Without spoiling, the game sets a dark, heavy tone, with cinematic cutscenes that feel like a movie.
The combination of Kojima’s directing, excellent voice acting, and intense atmosphere makes the short runtime feel dense and meaningful.[/b]

[h1]Visuals & Sound Design:[/h1]
[b]Powered by the FOX Engine, the game looks stunning, from detailed character models to the rain-soaked prison camp, the visuals immerse you completely. The guards’ chatter, the tension-filled silence when sneaking, and the sharp crack of suppressed gunfire all enhance the realism. Kiefer Sutherland as Snake also gives a grittier tone to the character.[/b]

[h1]Replayability & Extras:[/h1]
[b]Even though the campaign is short. Side Missions (Side Ops) that expand the sandbox experience. Different Difficulty Levels for hardcore stealth fans. Secrets & Collectibles for completionists. If you treat this as a stealth playground rather than just a short story, it offers way more than the two-hour runtime critics complain about.[/b]

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Smooth and refined stealth mechanics

[*]Beautiful FOX Engine graphics and realistic sound design

[*]Multiple approaches to missions encourage creativity

[*]Side Ops & challenges add replay value

[*]Serves as an excellent prologue to The Phantom Pain

[*]Classic Kojima cinematic storytelling
[/list]
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Very short main story (around 2 hours for the first playthrough)

[*]Could feel like “paid DLC” for some players

[*]Lack of mission variety compared to the full game

[*]Not for players who want long campaigns without replaying content
[/list]
[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
[b]Yes, Ground Zeroes is short. But short doesn’t mean bad. In fact, it’s an incredibly polished and memorable introduction to the world of The Phantom Pain. Every second is crafted with Kojima’s signature attention to detail.[/b]

[h1]Barebones explanation about this game. [b]This is not a demo![/b][/h1]

In the eve of [i]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain[/i], I'll be reviewing [i]Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes[/i] because some people still don't seem to get it at this point ([u]short version at the bottom of the review[/u]).

[b]First of all, I've played most of the MGS games before this and I love them to death, so my opinion may be a bit biased.[/b]

[i]Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes[/i] is a prologue to [i]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain[/i], like way back when there was a pretty short and limited Gran Turismo 5 Prologue but was still sold as a full game. That's not the case with [i]GZ[/i].

Bear with me for a moment, this game focuses on giving you a glimpse of what [i]The Phantom Pain[/i] will be. [i]GZ[/i] puts you in control of Snake (aka Big Boss) in an infiltration mission, but gives you the freedom to explore the mission area and tackle objectives as you see fit. With collectibles spread throughout the map, it invites you to step in every corner, watch enemy movements and memorize them, listen to soldiers' conversations, hijack vehicles, all adding up to the experience and helping you reach your goal. This main story centrical [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] mission, can take from anywhere between 15 minutes and 1 hour or more since there's no time limit, also depending if you go full stealth or guns blazing towards your objective. 

After you're done with the main mission, you unlock pseudo historical recreations of events prior to the [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] mission in forms of Side Operations. These Side Ops have different targets and goals, from eliminating 2 targets in the entire military base, to destroying enemy turrets just before an airstrike. All of them take place in the same area as the [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] mission, but you get a specific starting point for each one of them. Again, you're free to tackle your objectives however you see fit.

There are two more unlockable Side Ops which main feature is fan service. I could explain those two but why ruin the surprise? [spoiler]You can look online or in Steam for guides on how to unlock them anyway.[/spoiler]

If you're a fan of the games and story, there are little nods to the past of the series. If you're new to the series, these collectibles and tapes will show you part of a great cohesive plot that has been developed over some great games, hopefully ending you with trying the rest of the MGS games.

All in all $20 isn't overpriced because the content is there. It is locked behind extras, but taking into mind how it's possible to put to sleep an entire army with a tranquilizer gun, then run over them with a tank, [b]what you get is based on how and for how long you play[/b]. As of the moment of this review [i]Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes[/i] comes bundled for free with each pre-order of [i]Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain[/i], so you get to experience this game just before the main course is released.

[b]Short version:[/b]
[list]
[*]Ground Zeroes is a prologue game, not a demo
[*]Shows you the core mechanics of the upcoming Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
[*]Allows for replayability based on how you tackle objectives
[*]Has side missions with different objectives, with many ways to tackle them
[*]Many collectibles, some of them unlock more missions and story elements
[*]What you see in the game depends on how you play and for how long you play
[*]As of the moment of this review, [i]Ground Zeroes[/i] is free with each pre-order of [i]The Phantom Pain[/i]
[/list]

Thank you for your time, I hope this helps your decision of whether getting or not this game. Have fun!

Ground Zeroes is awesome and makes you instantly want to see what happens next in Game Of The Century, The Phantom Pain.

It is very easy to dismiss this game with a negative review as it only has one location where its missions take place. On the other hand, the description on the store page emphasises that Ground Zeroes is meant to be a prologue to the now available Phantom Pain. Basically, Ground Zeroes showcases the engine developed for Phantom Pain as well as its stealth gameplay.

[b]Snake in Cuba[/b]

We are in the '70s and Snake's job is to infiltrate a camp controlled by a paramilitary group where two hostages are being held. Basically, both are children and need to be exfiltrated before the enemy can get any information out of them. The intro looks great with the appearance of Skull Face - he looks quite menacing; he is basically the MGS version of Marvel's Red Skull. The ending gives us a rewarding cutscene that is also meant to be a sort of trailer for Phantom Pain.

[b]Gameplay at its best[/b]

Controlling Snake is very easy and we have the option to do a lot of things (in terms of movement, that is). The game focuses on stealth-based gameplay so if you prefer a more action-oriented approach this is not really for you. Imagine it as a kind of Splinter Cell game. Ending a mission results in an evaluation screen - not killing anybody and being unnoticed all the time can yield us the best score (labelled "S"). 

The game is not difficult. A so-called Reflex mode allows us to quickly react if we are noticed. The camera even directs us in the right way - doing a quick headshot (with a silencer on) can still save the day. I like how you can interrogate enemies making sure you get more information on the camp. This includes the location of ammo storage or information on where certain enemy types (e.g. snipers) are positioned. What I like about the main mission is how the order in which we save the children can be decided. 

[b]Replayability? Longevity?[/b]

This is the controversial part of Ground Zeroes. Once the main mission is completed (in roughly 2 hours) you realise you have seen everything. Although additional missions (4 of them, so-called Side Ops) are available they all take place in the same camp. Objectives are different, though. Some are easier (the Intel Op Rescue is action heavy where stealth is hardly an option), while some require several reloads (Destroy AA Emplacements can be quite tough). 

The above are varied and interesting but do not provide much additional information to the story. They do not change the fact that it is still not a full game; it is more like a stripped down AAA game which is not necessarily a problem, however, when you look at the regular price (20 EURs) it is understandable that some might see this as insulting.

[b]Conclusion[/b]

If I remember correctly I purchased the game with a 75% discount. This was the correct price for something that can be completed in a mere 2 hours of playtime. I was happy to keep playing to complete the extra missions for more achievements. Overall, the game looks and plays like an AAA game: it looks great, voice acting is also very good (I understand Kiefer Sutherland is a regular when it comes to Solid Snake's voice) and completing the Side Ops can be very challenging (with an "S" rank in mind). It wouldn't be a Kojima / Konami game without all the hidden easter eggs, collectibles and extra gameplay modes / levels. 

If you don't mind playing a "prologue" title then Ground Zeroes can be fun. Otherwise watch a playthrough on YouTube and head for Phantom Pain immediately.

As a huge MGS fan it's obvious I like this game. But what about those who never even touched an MGS game?

First off, this main game is short. Your first run on the main mission should take anywhere between 90 minutes or 3 hours at most. If you play just the main story and that's it, you'll be dissapointed. But if you like to complete side missions and have OCD, I feel you'll get your moneys worth with collecting all those XOF patches/cassette tapes, getting higher ranks, and finding new ways to complete missions.

As the for the gameplay, it's MGS at it's finest. Switching from crouching to crawling has never felt smoother, and it's actually hard to go back to something like MGS4 after playing this. And gunplay is great, especially with the new bullet drop effects, which makes you rethink about sniping someone across the map. My only complaint would have to be the cover mechanics. They're... quite awful to be honest. Hope they fix this in The Phantom Pain. Also no cardboard box. WTF?

The AI is pretty good as well. If you stand in broad daylight, it's obvious they'll see you 20 meters away, even on normal. And if you think reflex mode makes this game too easy, you're very mistaken. Especially when you get spotted by 3 guards and all you just shot a single shot tranq. Also, don't rely on regen health. Take too much damage, and you'll have to manually heal yourself with the marijuana health spray from Resident Evil. Realistic? No. But neither is eating rations that magically heal you after a point blank rocket launcher blast.

tl;dr version:

Pros are great replayability, lots of stuff to collect, gameplay, graphics, Hideo Kojima, and marijuana health spray.

Cons are short main mission, cover mechanics, no cardboard box, and too much water.

Overall I'd recommend this those who like to do everything in the game, have OCD, and want a great stealth experience.

Don't recommend if all you're here for is the main story. You'll feel ripped off. And hate water.

This is one of the most well made stealth game experiences I've ever played, It outshines the game it is meant to be a prologue for in many ways, namely in it's fantastic level design, music implementation, and difficulty.

Alright, let's talk about Ground Zeroes. Is it a full game? No. Does it feel like the best prologue ever made? Absolutely. If you’re a fan of sneaking around like a shadow and pulling off stealthy takedowns, then this is your playground.

The gameplay is tight—Snake moves like a panther, and the controls are super responsive. The open-world setting, even if it’s small compared to The Phantom Pain, gives you a lot of freedom to approach missions however you want. It’s the kind of game that lets you feel like a genius one minute, then laugh at your own mistakes the next.

But the elephant in the room: it’s short. Really short. You could finish the main mission in about an hour, but there’s a ton of replay value if you're into trying different tactics or completing side ops. Still, for what it is, it packs a punch. The tension, the atmosphere, the amazing voice work by Kiefer Sutherland—it's all there. It’s like a delicious appetizer that leaves you hungry for the full meal (which is The Phantom Pain).

If you're a hardcore MGS fan, it's a must-play. If you're new to the series, this might not sell you completely, but you'll appreciate the precision and care put into it. Just don’t expect a full course—this is Kojima giving you a taste of the chaos that’s to come.

Verdict: Bite-sized, but oh so satisfying.

Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is practically a demo for MGSV: The Phantom Pain, introducing the improved graphics and gameplay style, focusing heavily on stealth. There are 7 missions, but at start you can only play the first one, Ground Zeroes, which is the main story and prologue to TPP. After finishing it once you'll be able to play the other missions, and a secret one is unlocked by gathering all collectible badges in the main mission. 

All of these missions take place in the same map, which is kinda a good thing since you'll get more familiar in later runs. The differences other than enemy and item placement are only cosmetic, like weather and time of day. However, the 6 other missions have different objectives. There are the normal ones, such as assassination and intel gathering, and some weird, meta ones like recreating scenes from the first game and killing aliens.

I don't have a problem with this game only having 1 map since its basically a demo, but I don't like how difficult it is. Many areas are too open and enemies can spot you easily. Enemies don't stay knocked out as well. It gets harder when you have to carry someone out, like in the main mission. It also has no manual/quicksaving, only autosaves which can make you redo a part many times. However, it can also be a good thing, as it resets enemy position and detection, and can be easily re-triggered by crossing an area that triggered it before.

Overall, I think Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is a pretty decent stealth game, and it actually gets more fun and easier by the time you get more familiar with the maps. Just get Metal Gear Solid V: The Definitive Experience, as it contains both TPP and GZ with many DLCs. I do hope The Phantom Pain is easier though, as the difficulty can get a bit frustrating.

This fantastic, little game got a lot of criticism for being a ‘glorified demo’, for Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain. People said that it should have been released for free and that it was just a cheap way to ‘cash in’ on the Metal Gear hype. However, as you would expect from Hideo Kojima and his team, Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is a masterpiece, in it’s own right.

The layers of detail and purposefully built in replay value, make this ‘single area’ game, well worth your time (and money). It is loaded with ‘fan service’ and ‘Easter eggs’, with lots of references to previous games in the series. This version also includes all the DLC, which were previously exclusive to different consoles, before the PC release. It also runs flawlessly for me on a GTX980 running Windows 10.

I really enjoy the gameplay style of Ground Zeroes which requires you to revisit the same environment, many times, in multiple different ways. It encourages me to further appreciate the immersive atmosphere and attention to detail in this single environment. In fact, I got hooked on Ground Zeroes a lot quicker than I did with Phantom Pain, which I still haven’t finished. 

Considering that Kojima’s creative process was interfered with during the completion of Phantom Pain. Ground Zeroes seems more like a sincere Metal Gear experience than Phantom Pain is. I love this game and that’s what Ground Zeroes is in my opinion, a full game, that stands strong on it’s own. It’s an excellent, fully fleshed out masterpiece, which (considering it’s size) is filled with great content.

Finally, another Metal Gear Solid comes to PC, this time back to its routes of being a stealthy tactical title which is a far cry from the type of game REVENGEANCE was.

The stealthy aspect of Ground Zeroes does everything right. It's something that the whole series does well, so it should be expected though. As I have only had the experience with MGS 1, 2, Snake Eater and Revengeance, the melee controls seem fluid and faultless. All in all, the combat system and stealth are amazing, and I wouldn't change anything about them. 

Now, I seem to be saying this every time I review a big AAA game, but these are some absolutely gorgeous graphics, whack all the settings up to full and you are looking at an actual piece of artwork. I couldn't believe how real the world looks in here. The character models, faces, everything, this game really shows off the power of PC gaming. 

Ground Zeroes is the prologue for a future MGS title, Phantom Pane, although I understand Phantom Pane is going to be a much bigger title, I still felt a little miffed off that I was paying £16,99 for a game that only lasted two hours, and that's with doing the extra missions at the end. The actual main story can be completed in less than an hour if you know what you are doing....this to me was the only negative point from this release. 

I had no technical issues at all, it's quite surprising to see a developer who mainly makes games for consoles, push out such a well-made port. A nice, steady, 60 fps the whole time playing. 

The final verdict on Ground Zeroes; I would recommend it, but maybe wait until it drops on sale so you don't feeling the same as I did with regards to the game's length. If it wasn't for that, I'd say this is a must buy and a great game to test your rigs on.

METAL GEAR SOLID V: Ground Zeroes is a stealth-based third-person shooter.
Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes is the prologue to Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain.
Set in 1975, a few months after the events of Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker, the story follows the legendary hero Snake (Big Boss) who infiltrates a Cuban military base to rescue hostages.
It is the typical Metal Gear Solid scheme, the Player controls Snake through the game map and attempt to complete missions while avoiding being spotted by the enemy.
However, it is the first Metal Gear game with an kinda open world experience, which really adds a lot of variability to the Metal Gear Solid Series.
Unfortunately the story ends already after finishing the first mission. Everything after is about looking for collectables or doing "Challenges".
The graphics are pretty awesome, nothing really to complain about.
The voice acting, sounds and music are perfect.
The controls are easy to work with, and the gameplay is very well done.
From my point of view with 19,99 Euro it is totaly overpriced. You should get it within a sale or buy the METAL GEAR SOLID V: The Definitive Experience, where you can get Metal Gear Solid V: Ground Zeroes and Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain with all DLC's together.
Overall it is a good short introduction to Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain.
